A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same public-defense retrieval study. The full text, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching v3 Tables A1–A11 to v4 Tables 3–13 despite renaming and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original defender feedback, annotation analyses, a NotebookLM evaluation, and retrieval, fine-tuning and reranker experiments in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations, including retrieval scores in Table 2, reranker results in Figure 5, and detailed experiments in appendix Tables 7–12.

M1.justification: Dense retrieval, reranking, synthetic-query generation and filtering, IRAC expansion, and domain adaptation remain the same. Renaming the system, attributing the checkpoint, and omitting the recency-sorting description do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same NJOPD and public PD corpora, BarExam-QA, LePaRD, synthetic training datasets and US case-law domain adaptation. The public benchmark still contains 170 queries, 96,032 paragraphs and 543 annotated relevant paragraphs.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the eight pretrained retrievers, four fine-tuned retriever families, ModernBERT/Legal-ModernBERT pair, six off-the-shelf rerankers, fine-tuned Qwen reranker and majority baseline. Model-name clarifications do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the initial filtering-judge designation from GPT-4 to GPT-4o. Since v3 already mentions GPT-4o later in that passage, this is a limited correction to the reported preprocessing setting, not evidence of rerunning dataset construction. Splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 Section 5.1 omits the additional comparison between non-anonymized PD and proprietary OPD correlations reported in v3. The principal anonymization, temporal-subset, alternative-metric, synthetic-data and domain-adaptation analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Five seeded fine-tuning runs, 95% confidence intervals, correlation p-values and the domain-adaptation significance convention were already reported in v3. These reporting practices remain in v4, including Tables 8 and 10.

E6.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported fine-tuning Spearman R from 0.84 to 0.82. Section 5.2 changes majority-baseline F1 from 80.02 to 80.3, matching the retained figure and table. The extra non-anonymized-PD versus OPD correlation statement is removed. Corresponding numerical performance-table entries otherwise remain unchanged; these edits do not establish performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal query-to-paragraph retrieval definition in Section 2.3 is unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a realistic defender-retrieval benchmark and taxonomy, evidence of benchmark mismatch, and benefits from domain knowledge and query expansion. The system rename does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds automated GPT-4o/Qwen filtering as a potential source of benchmark bias in the broader-impact statement. Table 6 newly suggests that the weaker recent-subset correlation reflects small sample size and calls R=0.61, p=0.108 marginally significant; v3 Table A4 reports those numbers without that interpretation.

D1.justification: v4 restores concrete anonymization and annotation examples, identifies the domain-adapted checkpoint's source, discloses exclusion of documents lacking year information, and specifies secure NJ State deployment restricted to NJOPD attorneys. The explicit recency-sorting description is removed. Dataset and replication links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Stammbach and Henderson (2026), attributing the domain-adapted ModernBERT checkpoint to that work instead of describing its pretraining as performed here. Broader research positioning remains stable; most other citation changes concern formatting.

P1.justification: v4 consistently renames NJ BriefBank to OPD Resource Library, standardizes terminology, tightens prose, corrects cross-references and adopts author-year citations. The main section sequence and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset, changing the title, author and abstract layout, typography, spacing and table presentation. Table captions move above displays with explanatory notes below, and appendix displays are resized and regrouped. Existing plots remain, with label and caption edits such as Figure 4's matching OPD becoming PD Dataset.

improvement.justification: Clearer checkpoint attribution, concrete prompt examples, acknowledgment of filtering bias, and correction of the majority-baseline F1 provide modest gains in transparency and accuracy. The empirical evidence is unchanged. Loss of the recency-sorting detail and the stronger, weakly supported interpretation of the p=0.108 temporal result limit the improvement.
